findings.checklist_item: - [ ] State the rationale reconciling the ownership-based carve-out with the approval gate's non-locality/shared-system basis (why own-tracker writeback is acceptable even though the tracker is shared), so the two sentences are provably consistent rather than merely asserted non-contradictory.
evidence: Plan: 'the tracker the debug session is already operating within … is "the project's own mandated tracker" and receives the prescribed writebacks un-gated; ANY other tracker is third-party and stays approval-gated.'
SKILL.md:99: 'Seek explicit user approval before any action that mutates a non-local or shared system, including … writing/transitioning/commenting on Jira or other trackers'
The gate's discriminator is locality/shared-ness; the plan's carve-out discriminator is ownership — these are different axes, so 'no contradiction' is asserted, not shown.
findings.finding: The inline tracker discriminator ungates writebacks on an OWNERSHIP axis ('the project's own mandated tracker'), but the existing approval gate it amends is justified on a NON-LOCALITY / shared-system basis ('any action that mutates a non-local or shared system … writing/transitioning/commenting on Jira or other trackers'). An own-project Jira is still a shared system others read; the plan asserts the carve-out produces 'no contradiction' but does not state why own-tracker mutation is safe against the gate's own stated rationale.
scenarios: A debug session operating within a shared team Jira writes RCA/summary comments un-gated; other consumers of that shared tracker see mutations the original gate intended to require approval for.
findings.suggested_fix: Add one sentence to change (14)'s rationale: the own-tracker writebacks are exactly the artifacts the debug session is mandated to produce for the ticket it was invoked on, so they are in-scope work product rather than an unscoped mutation of an unrelated shared system — which is the risk the gate targets.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Specify what the tracker discriminator resolves to and how the four writebacks behave when the debug session has no ticket/tracker under debug (e.g. writebacks no-op; RCA/summary live only in the Reporting message).
evidence: Plan: discriminator = 'the tracker … that produced or holds the ticket under debug'.
SKILL.md:25-26: 'The input is a problem or a list of problems (a bug report, a failing test, a stack trace, an incident, a Jira ticket, a vague "X is broken").'
No plan text covers the ticket-less / tracker-less input case.
findings.finding: The tracker discriminator and the writeback lifecycle are anchored to 'the ticket under debug', but the skill explicitly accepts inputs with no ticket or tracker (a failing test, a stack trace, a vague 'X is broken'). The plan does not state what the discriminator resolves to, or whether the writebacks no-op, when there is no ticket/tracker under debug.
scenarios: A user invokes /rebar-debug on a bare stack trace with no ticket: the four writebacks have no target and the 'own tracker' discriminator has no referent.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Pin which writebacks fire on the not-a-bug exit path (classification comment always; RCA comment if a mechanism was proven; and that the fix-shaped Reporting-summary writeback does NOT fire when there is no fix), mapping each to its lifecycle point.
evidence: Plan: writebacks = 'Phase-1-exit RCA comment', 'Reporting summary comment (cause/proof/test/fix/siblings/replication)', 'not-a-bug classification comment + cited source' — anchored to lifecycle points.
SKILL.md:396-404: not-a-bug classifications 'stop; do not auto-apply a fix … hand the decision to the user' — so no test/fix/siblings/replication exist to summarize.
The Reporting summary writeback's fields (test/fix/siblings/replication) are undefined on the not-a-bug exit.
findings.finding: The not-a-bug path exits before Phase 2 and hands the decision to the user (Steps 4-7 never run, and there is a distinct not-a-bug Reporting block). The plan lists a not-a-bug classification writeback but does not state whether the Phase-1-exit RCA comment and the Reporting summary comment writebacks also fire on this path, nor which lifecycle point they attach to when no fix/Step-7 sweep exists.
scenarios: Legitimacy resolves to intended-behavior: there is a confirmed mechanism and a classification, but no fix, test, or Step-7 sweep — which of the writebacks are due, and in what shape?

findings.finding: The writeback approach hinges on classifying a tracker as 'the project's own mandated tracker' (prescribed, un-gated writebacks) vs. 'third-party' (approval-gated), but the plan states no rule the agent can apply to make that determination in an arbitrary client project — and it silently amends the existing hard fail-safe (SKILL.md L99-100 gates 'writing/transitioning/commenting on Jira or other trackers').
findings.location: Approach, change (14) 'Approval-gate reconciliation'; against SKILL.md L99-100
findings.suggested_fix: Define the discriminator inline (e.g., the tracker the skill is already operating within / the one that produced the ticket under debug is the 'own mandated tracker'; any other named tracker is third-party), and add an explicit sentence amending the Approval-gate section so it does not contradict the prescribed writebacks.

findings.finding: The approval-gate reconciliation distinguishes 'the project's own mandated tracker' (gets prescribed writebacks) from 'third-party trackers' (stay approval-gated), but the plan does not state how the executing skill DECIDES which tracker a given project's is — leaving the discriminator to the executor.
findings.suggested_fix: Add one clause defining the test, e.g.: 'the project's own mandated tracker' = the tracker the project's configured workflow requires; absent such a declaration, treat as third-party and apply the approval gate.

evidence: 2 criterion line(s) bundle multiple deliverables with 'and' (split so each is independently verifiable).
findings.suggested_fix: Split compound criteria, replace subjective terms with observable outcomes, and state how each is verified.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Bound axis 2's entry condition so it fires only when the fixed code genuinely sits on a shared core with multiple parallel surfaces (not merely because facades exist), and reconcile the broadened OR trigger with the 'scale the ceremony to the bug' no-op-for-local-fixes stance.
evidence: Plan: 'enter when the root cause is a repeatable construct pattern (axis 1) OR when the fixed code sits on one of several parallel surfaces (axis 2 — a parity sibling is an absence, present even for one-off constructs)'.
SKILL.md:50-51: 'the anti-pattern sweep runs only when the cause is a repeatable pattern' — named as a conditional gate meant to no-op for average bugs.
SKILL.md:53-54: 'An average happy-path bug should feel light — don't … [run] sweeps a single-site fix doesn't warrant.'
findings.finding: Axis 2's entry condition ('the fixed code sits on one of several parallel surfaces … present even for one-off constructs'), OR-ed into the Step-7 trigger, could fire the 5-slot channel census on most fixes that touch code with multiple surfaces (CLI/MCP/library). This widens a gate the skill's 'Scale the ceremony to the bug' principle deliberately keeps conditional and no-op for average bugs; the plan does not reconcile or bound the broadened trigger against that principle.
findings.location: Approach (15); SKILL.md:47-55 ('Scale the ceremony to the bug'), 553-557 (Step 7 trigger)
scenarios: A single-site fix in a module that has CLI/MCP/library facades trips axis 2's 'parallel surfaces' condition and forces a full 5-slot channel census, contrary to the light-touch stance for local fixes.

findings.finding: The Scope line asserts a 'symlinked copy' of rebar-debug/SKILL.md that must be kept consistent, but no such symlink or second copy exists in the repo, and the project's own convention for shared skill files is byte-identical real-file copies (via `cp`), not symlinks.
findings.location: Scope section: 'examples/agent-skills/rebar-debug/SKILL.md (+ symlinked copy consistency; ~35-45 lines total)'
findings.suggested_fix: Remove the 'symlinked copy consistency' clause from Scope; SKILL.md exists once as a real file. If a genuine second copy exists in a target harness path, name that exact path and cite it; otherwise scope is the single file examples/agent-skills/rebar-debug/SKILL.md.

findings.finding: The plan's Scope names a '(+ symlinked copy consistency)' obligation and Testing names 'skill-file lint/sync checks if present' for SKILL.md, but no synced/symlinked copy of SKILL.md exists. The repo's only skill-sync gate (tests/unit/test_skill_shared_sync.py) and the README both scope byte-identical copying to shared/test-design.md exclusively; each skill's SKILL.md is a unique per-directory file with no sync partner.
findings.location: Scope ('examples/agent-skills/rebar-debug/SKILL.md (+ symlinked copy consistency)') and Testing ('skill-file lint/sync checks if present')
findings.suggested_fix: Change Scope to name only 'examples/agent-skills/rebar-debug/SKILL.md' and reword Testing to run the existing skill sync/lint gate (make test / test_skill_shared_sync.py) as a regression check only — noting SKILL.md itself is not a synced copy — rather than implying an SKILL.md sync obligation.

findings.finding: Change 15 adds a second Step-7 axis with its own trigger ('only when fixed code sits on one of several parallel surfaces'), but Step 7 as written is entered only under the existing trigger ('Run this only when the root cause is a repeatable pattern', SKILL.md L555). A parity sibling is an ABSENCE on a parallel surface — not a recurring construct — so under the existing gate the new axis is skipped exactly when it applies. The plan does not state how the two triggers compose at the single Step-7 entry point.
findings.location: Approach, change (15) 'Trigger: only when fixed code sits on one of several parallel surfaces'; against SKILL.md L555
findings.suggested_fix: Reword the Step-7 entry so each axis carries its own independent trigger and the step is entered when either fires; run axis-1 when its trigger holds and axis-2 when its trigger holds.
